search_bias: Continue from unresolved clean frontier outside mainstream agent literature. This run prioritized simulation-optimization budget allocation, dual control/active system identification, distributed straggler mitigation, then sparse statistical debugging. Prefer matched baselines, quantitative effects, explicit scope, and transferable mechanism abstraction.

candidates_new.mechanism: Optimal computing budget allocation (OCBA): allocate stochastic evaluation replications unevenly according to estimated design separation/noise so that the probability of correct selection rises faster than under equal allocation.
candidates_new.primary_source: Shi, Chen, Yücesan, Simultaneous Simulation Experiments and Nested Partition for Discrete Resource Allocation in Supply Chain Management, Winter Simulation Conference 1999, https://www.informs-sim.org/wsc99papers/055.PDF
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: For a reduced 210-design stochastic resource-allocation problem, 10,000 independent experiments were used to estimate probability of correct selection. Reaching P{CS}=99% required computation budget 14,600 with OCBA versus 330,000 with equal simulation allocation, reported as a speedup as high as 23 and about 96% reduction in required simulation time in that setting.
candidates_new.scope: A specific supply-chain/discrete-resource-allocation simulation study with known benchmark structure and a reduced 210-design subproblem. The 23x factor is not a universal OCBA speedup and finite-budget pathologies are known in later literature.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: When candidate mechanisms must be repeatedly evaluated under stochastic seeds/tasks, dynamically concentrate evaluation budget on designs whose uncertainty and mean gaps make them decision-critical instead of allocating equal repetitions to every branch. Pair with racing/elimination rather than treating OCBA as a universal fixed allocation rule.
candidates_new.confidence: high for original result; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Dual control / active model discrimination: choose actions not only for immediate control performance but also for how informative their resulting observations will be about uncertain model structure, with probing automatically fading as uncertainty falls.
candidates_new.primary_source: Heirung, Santos, Mesbah, Model predictive control with active learning for stochastic systems with structural model uncertainty: Online model discrimination, Computers & Chemical Engineering 128 (2019) 128-140, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compchemeng.2019.05.012 ; open manuscript https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10180013
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: In the nonlinear bioreactor structural-change case, active-learning MPC selected the correct model 8.1 h after the change versus 15.5 h for passive learning, a reported 47.7% reduction in time to correct model selection. The paper also compares against nominal MPC, robust MPC without learning, and passive-learning MPC, while noting approximation limits in its Bayes-risk surrogate.
candidates_new.scope: Simulation case study on nonlinear bioreactor control with a finite hypothesis set and explicit structural change; this is not evidence that dual control gives the same improvement in arbitrary research loops.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Research actions can be scored partly by whether their outcomes discriminate among competing mechanism hypotheses, not only by expected immediate benchmark gain. Prefer experiments with high decision-sensitive information value, then reduce exploration bonuses once model uncertainty is low.
candidates_new.confidence: high for original model-discrimination result; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Cause- and resource-aware straggler mitigation: detect slow tasks early, distinguish causes, and choose among restart, duplicate, network-aware placement, or output protection using opportunity/resource cost rather than blindly cloning all laggards.
candidates_new.primary_source: Ananthanarayanan et al., Reining in the Outliers in Map-Reduce Clusters using Mantri, OSDI 2010, https://www.usenix.org/event/osdi10/tech/full_papers/osdi10_proceedings.pdf
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Deployment in a Bing production cluster plus trace-driven simulation reported about 32% average job-completion improvement. The paper reports 21% and 42% faster job phases at the 50th and 75th percentiles in simulation; median completion-time reduction improved 3.1x over the next-best scheme while using fewer resources. Preferential output replication sped up half of jobs by at least 20% with about 1% extra network traffic. Production copies succeeded 2.8x more often while 0.47x as many copies were launched compared with the earlier build.
candidates_new.scope: Large MapReduce-style production clusters with task/phase structure and measurable progress. Some gains combine multiple Mantri mechanisms, so do not attribute the full 32% to a single restart/replication rule.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For parallel research workers, diagnose why a branch is slow or stuck before taking recovery action. Restart or duplicate only when expected time saved exceeds extra resource cost; protect expensive intermediate artifacts when recomputation risk dominates; account for shared bottlenecks rather than treating all stalls as identical.
candidates_new.confidence: high for original systems result; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Sparse randomized diagnostic instrumentation: sample a tiny unbiased fraction of potential internal predicates across many executions, then use aggregate failure correlation to localize problematic behavior with low runtime overhead.
candidates_new.primary_source: Benjamin Liblit, Cooperative Bug Isolation dissertation and project, 2004, https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~liblit/dissertation/
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: A bc-1.06 crash case used 2,729 runs with roughly 9 MB random inputs and monitored 30,150 predicates over 8,910 lines. Sampling was key to practicality: a cited measurement gives about 13% overhead without sampling versus about 0.5% overhead at a 1/1000 sampling rate for that diagnostic setup. The dissertation validates statistical-debugging methods across case studies, including previously unknown crashing bugs.
candidates_new.scope: Post-deployment software debugging and predicate instrumentation; the cited overhead/case figures do not establish a universal localization-time reduction, and performance depends on many executions to aggregate sparse observations.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Instead of recording every internal detail of every research run, randomly sample lightweight diagnostic features across many runs and correlate them with success/failure. This may preserve causal observability while keeping logging/context overhead low enough for continuous deployment.
candidates_new.confidence: medium-high for original low-overhead observability mechanism; medium-low for transfer

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Rejected. The 14,600 versus 330,000 result is a scoped resource-allocation simulation case; finite-budget OCBA can underperform equal allocation in some regimes, so only the adaptive-budget principle is transferable without further validation.

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Rejected in favor of Mantri's cause- and resource-aware policy; its evaluation explicitly reports fewer copies, higher copy success, and lower completion time than prior cloning-style approaches.

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Deferred. Primary evidence strongly supports low-overhead sparse instrumentation and successful case localization, but this run did not obtain a clean matched reduction in human diagnosis trials or localization entropy.
